official_measurement_examples.name: Knotweed on land
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency guidance states you do not legally have to remove Japanese knotweed from your land unless it is causing a nuisance, but you must stop it spreading off your property.

official_measurement_examples.name: Causing spread
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government guidance states you can be prosecuted for causing Japanese knotweed or other listed invasive plants to grow or spread in the wild.

official_measurement_examples.name: Contaminated soil
official_measurement_examples.fact: Soil or plant material contaminated with Japanese knotweed may be controlled waste and must not be treated as ordinary surplus soil.

official_measurement_examples.name: Off-site disposal
official_measurement_examples.fact: Off-site knotweed disposal must use an appropriately permitted landfill or incineration facility and a registered waste carrier.

official_measurement_examples.name: On-site burial
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government guidance sets specific notification, depth and membrane conditions for permitted on-site burial routes; these are waste controls rather than planning approvals.

official_measurement_examples.name: IAS A02 scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: IAS A02 permits specified management activities for listed invasive species only for eradication, control or containment and within licence conditions.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 herbicide update
official_measurement_examples.fact: The invasive-plant guidance was updated 12 February 2026 to link the England online herbicide-agreement service for use in or near water.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Invasive-plant presence, management plans, waste controls and species licences do not themselves determine planning permission, ownership or parcel development capacity.

core_rules: Japanese knotweed presence is not automatic planning refusal
planning permission does not authorise unlawful invasive-plant spread
absence of a legal removal duty is not permission to cause spread
knotweed-contaminated soil is not ordinary surplus soil
waste carrier registration is not planning permission
permitted landfill acceptance is not parcel remediation approval
IAS A02 management licence is not land-use permission
A03 release licence is distinct from IAS A02 management licence
herbicide agreement near water is not planning permission
historic knotweed treatment record must retain dates and treated area
plant management plan is not proof eradication is complete
invasive plant control does not determine land ownership
Schedule 9 listing is not proof the species is present on a parcel
treatment compliance does not reserve development capacity
no parcel invasive-plant clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
